scope.existingUniverse: All ideas re-screened against developments since the prior run; differentiated exposures preferred over duplicates.

keyChange.reason: SLB signed a $4.1B enterprise-value acquisition of Kelvion, converting an oilfield-services name into a meaningful data-centre thermal-management crossover. Pro-forma 2026 data-centre revenue exceeds $2B with ~$300M adjusted EBITDA; management targets $4.5-5.0B revenue and $700-800M adjusted EBITDA in 2028. Purchase price is ~11x estimated 2026 EBITDA pre-synergies/~8.5x including run-rate synergies; SLB expects EPS/FCF-per-share accretion in year one and net debt/EBITDA within its <=1.5x target. This is sufficiently differentiated to raise priority, but integration and execution prevent a core-tier promotion today.

macro.summary: Higher-rate/inflation risk and geopolitical energy volatility still argue for cash generation and valuation discipline. The strongest structural evidence continues to sit in physical AI infrastructure: power, grid, cooling, water, networking and advanced packaging. Do not rely on the stale Macro Stack feed.
macro.hardAssets: Gold/BTC remain useful long-duration monetary/debasement candidates but are outside the core Power Stack equity hierarchy; oil remains more cyclical/self-limiting at extreme prices, so integrated/refining/logistics and infrastructure exposures are preferred to indiscriminate upstream beta.
macro.nextCheckpoint: August ISM Manufacturing is scheduled for 2026-09-01 10:00 ET, after this run; July remains the latest officially released dataset at capture time. August Services is due 2026-09-03 10:00 ET.

powerGrid.read: GEV/PWR/ETN/TNB/MNHLDG/SCGBHD remain preferred physical bottleneck exposures. No new evidence justified a base-conviction change before the August ISM release.

aiDataCentres.read: SLB/Kelvion is the key new development. Cooling is becoming strategic enough for a major oilfield-services company to commit $4.1B EV and target $4.5-5B of data-centre revenue by 2028. This reinforces the thesis that scarce enabling infrastructure can capture AI capex without owning GPU economics directly.

nuclear.read: BWXT Janus remains the strongest fresh confirmation: the Army selected BWXT Advanced Nuclear Reactor technology for Fort Campbell, while Project Pele is already in manufacturing toward 2028 operation. Operating nuclear/components/fuel remain preferable to pre-commercial concept equities.

uraniumFuel.read: No fresh contract/supply evidence since the prior run cleared the bar for CCJ/LEU hierarchy changes. HALEU/TRISO scarcity remains strategically relevant through Janus/Pele.

oilGas.read: SLB is now more differentiated than a conventional upstream-services thesis because Kelvion adds data-centre thermal management. XOM remains the higher-quality owned energy anchor; do not chase war-premium crude mechanically.

metals.read: Copper remains structurally supported by grid/data-centre/electrification demand, but high prices increase capex and margin risk for downstream equipment contractors. Prefer bottleneck-linked producers/equipment suppliers with pricing power over broad China reflation beta.

roboticsAutomation.read: Fresh China evidence still shows scale in humanoid shipments but weak factory-job readiness. Shipment volume alone does not overturn the commercial ROI advantage of fixed automation, machine vision and established industrial controls.
